# Hall Safety Rules
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Scope
1.1 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
1.2 They apply to all hirers, trustees, visitors and contractors.
1.3 The named hirer must explain emergency exits to organisers.

## 2. Fire safety
2.1 All marked fire exits must remain unobstructed.
2.2 Fire doors must not be wedged open.
2.3 Open flames, candles and fireworks are prohibited.
2.4 Electrical appliances brought in must be safe and undamaged.
2.5 Cooking is permitted only in the designated kitchen.
2.6 No cooking equipment may be placed in hired rooms.

## 3. Occupancy and supervision
3.1 Maximum numbers are specified in hall-bookings.md section 4.
3.2 The hirer must count attendees when an event begins.
3.3 Children under 12 must remain under adult supervision.
3.4 At least one responsible adult must remain near the main entrance.
3.5 Corridors and access routes must remain clear.

## 4. Emergencies and reporting
4.1 In a fire, occupants must evacuate immediately.
4.2 Emergency services must be contacted when necessary.
4.3 Occupants must assemble at the marked garden gate.
4.4 Nobody may re-enter until emergency services permit it.
4.5 Injuries requiring first aid must be recorded in the incident book.
4.6 Serious incidents must be reported to the chair within 24 hours.

## 5. Emergency spending
5.1 The chair may authorise up to £400 for urgent safety work.
5.2 This exception overrides hall-trustees.md section 5.2.
5.3 A second trustee must confirm the urgency in writing.
5.4 The spending must be reported at the next committee meeting.

## 6. Temporary closure
6.1 The chair may close an unsafe room immediately.
6.2 A closed room must not be hired until declared safe.
6.3 Refunds caused by safety closure follow hall-refunds.md section 3.

# Booking Desk Quick Guide
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Using this guide
This sheet was last refreshed on 10 July 2026.
It is a convenience summary, not a governing document.
The governing documents and hall-changes.md always prevail.
Check the event and cancellation dates before quoting a price.

## 2. Rooms and prices
The Main Hall normally costs £28 an hour.
The Meeting Room costs £12 an hour.
The kitchen costs another £8 per booking.
Bookings normally last at least two hours per room.
Registered village groups generally get 25% off room hire.
Projectors cost £15 and portable speakers cost £10.
Display boards cost £5 per set.
Equipment and kitchen charges do not receive the group discount.

## 3. Booking and payment
Bookings can be requested up to a year ahead.
Allow at least three days before the event.
A booking is not accepted until confirmed in writing.
A £30 booking deposit is normally required.
The outstanding hire bill is generally due two weeks before the event.
Alcohol events also need a £100 damage deposit.

## 4. Opening and attendance
Monday to Thursday events now finish by 21:30.
Friday and Saturday events may run until 23:00.
Sunday events finish by 21:00.
The Main Hall holds up to 90 people.
The Meeting Room holds up to 24 people.
Combined events are limited to 100 people in the building.

## 5. Music and cancellations
Friday and Saturday amplified music stops at 21:30.
Music stops by 21:00 on other days.
Early cancellation may qualify for a full or partial refund.
Mid-range cancellations now generally receive 25% rather than 50%.
The booking deposit is normally kept when a hirer cancels.

## 6. Questions to refer
Check hall-refunds.md before promising any repayment.
Refer safety issues immediately to a trustee.
Do not settle disputed damage charges at the booking desk.

- Section 4.4 says capacities include organisers, performers and children, so the 89 and the 23 both count in full.
- 89 + 23 = 112 people, which is 12 over the 100 limit.

To fit, the organiser would need to cut the total attendance by at least 12 people. They would also have to stay within each room's own limit.
